title: A cult is divine which treats its object as present everywhere and able to hear every silent prayer at once
source_text: XXIII. Proinde cultus ipsis divinus est, qui supponit eum qui colitur, licet ipse sit inconspectus, nec sensibus ullis expositus, nihilominus omnes ipsum colentes, quovis tempore & loco, tanquam praesentem intueri; & quamvis, vel ab innumeris, ubivis terrarum dispersis hominibus, diversissimis votis simul rogetur atque invocetur, omnium tamen vota, etiam quae sola mente concepta sunt, percipere & intelligere, & singulis quam ab ipso petunt opem, uno momento ferre posse. Etiamsi qui cultu hujusmodi utitur, illum quem ita colit profiteatur se non habere pro Deo, sed tantum pro Dei amico & ministro, in quo se summum ipsum Deum honorare cogitet: quia quicquid homines fingere & praesumere possint, revera tanta majestas & potestas nulli competit, nisi Deo.
pass_a_gloss: Hence a cult is divine, for them, which supposes that the one who is cultivated, although he is unseen and exposed to no senses, nevertheless beholds as present all who cultivate him, at any time and place; and although he is asked and invoked at once with the most diverse vows even by innumerable men scattered everywhere on earth, he can yet perceive and understand the vows of all, even those conceived by the mind alone, and in one moment bring to each the help they seek from him. Even if the one who uses a cult of this sort professes that he does not take the one he thus cultivates for God, but only for a friend and minister of God, in whom he thinks he honors the supreme God himself: because, whatever men may imagine and presume, so great a majesty and power really belongs to none but God.
pass_b_english: Divine cult, on this account, treats its object as watching every worshiper, in every place and time, though unseen.
It also treats that object as hearing countless different prayers at once, including unspoken ones, and as able to help each person in a single moment.
Calling the object only God's friend and minister does not change the act.
Majesty and power of that size belong to God alone, whatever people imagine.

choices.why: The Roman excuse is named and refused as a redescription of divine power.
rejected: a fellow creature who is merely remembered
